#### Slide 03 — The Barbecue Stall Story

- **Title**: Two Kinds of People at a Barbecue Stall
- **Content**:
  - Left: The newly promoted person—opens by talking about resources, connections, and projects; onlookers flatter him verbally while calculating silently
  - Right: Another man—says little, asks only the key questions, and has figured out seven or eight tenths of everyone’s hand by the time they leave
  - Bottom: "Many games in this world are not lost because of a lack of ability, but because people reveal their abilities too soon"

#### Slide 04 — What Is Concealing One’s Talent

- **Layout**: Three-column cards (page_rhythm: dense)
- **Title**: Concealing your strengths ≠ playing dumb ≠ giving up
- **Content**: Three core actions
  - Put your sharpness away
  - Keep your desires in check
  - Move yourself out of the center of other people’s attention

#### Slide 05 — The Tree That Stands Out in the Forest

- **Layout**: Full-bleed + large centered quotation (page_rhythm: breathing)
- **Title**: (Quotation page, no subtitle)
- **Content**: "When a tree stands out in the forest, the wind will destroy it" — *增广贤文*
- Interpretation: When your strength is not yet enough to protect you, standing out becomes a risk

### Part 3: Common Errors

#### Slide 06 — The Mistake Young People Make Most Easily

- **Layout**: 2x2 grid cards + one sentence at the bottom (page_rhythm: dense)
- **Title**: Mistaking "Being Seen" for "Being Respected"
- **Content**:
  - The moment they achieve a little, they want everyone to know
  - The moment they gain some resources, they cannot resist showing them off
  - The moment they see through a little of human nature, they rush to expose it
  - Bottom: People in the spotlight have no cover; every probe, envy, attempt to leverage them, and act of sabotage comes their way first

#### Slide 07 — How to Hide Your Weaknesses

- **Layout**: Three-column comparison + quote at bottom (page_rhythm: dense)
- **Title**: Don’t waste your edge on small stages
- **Content**:
  - At dinners — Don’t interrupt
  - In meetings — Don’t rush to take a position
  - In a crowd — Don’t hurry to flaunt your connections
  - Bottom: “Silence is not emptiness; it is gathering information. Yielding is not weakness; it is refusing to waste ammunition on worthless targets.”

### Part 4: Historical Evidence

#### Slide 08 — Han Xin’s Humiliation Under the Legs

- **Layout**: Full-bleed image on the right + text on the left (page_rhythm: anchor)
- **Title**: Han Xin's Humiliation Under the Crotch
- **Content**:
  - Not to glorify humiliation
  - But because he refused to stake his life on a street confrontation
  - Winning the small battle might only vent one's anger; winning the larger game earns the chance to turn one's life around

#### Slide 09 — The Art of Concealing One's Strengths

- **Layout**: Four-row table (`page_rhythm: dense`)
- **Title**: Turn “Clumsiness” into a Shield
- **Content**: Performance × Others’ Reactions, four-row comparison
  - Too smart → They guard against you
  - Too forceful → They avoid you
  - Too eager → Resource holders drive down your price
  - Too determined to win → Opponents drag you into the game
  - Bottom: Being a little slower, duller, and more understated can actually reduce unnecessary exhaustion

#### Slide 10 — The Hidden Dragon Awaits Its Time

- **Layout**: Full-bleed + centered quotation (page_rhythm: breathing)
- **Title**: (Quotation page)
- **Content**: "The hidden dragon must not act" — *易经*
- Interpretation: When the dragon is in the abyss, it is not without power; the time has simply not yet come

### Part 5: Distinguishing the Differences

#### Slide 11 — Concealing One’s Strengths ≠ Passive Withdrawal from the World

- **Layout**: pros_cons_chart, two-column comparison (page_rhythm: dense)
- **Title**: Concealing your strengths ≠ passive withdrawal from the world
- **Visualization**: pros_cons_chart
- **Content**: Four-dimensional comparison
  - Motivation: passivity = fear of losing vs concealing your strengths = preparing to win
  - State: passivity = the more you hide, the weaker you become vs concealing your strengths = the more you hide, the deeper you grow
  - Silence: passivity = an excuse vs concealing your strengths = gathering strength
  - Inner world: passivity = resentment vs concealing your strengths = strategic positioning

#### Slide 12 — The Zeng Guofan Archetype

- **Layout**: Image left + text right (page_rhythm: anchor)
- **Title**: Zeng Guofan: The Hard Work, Slow Work, and Deep Work
- **Content**:
  - He was not known for his intelligence early in life and was even considered slow-witted
  - What he relied on: hard work / slow work / deep work
  - He did not chase momentary speed or grasp for the slightest clever shortcut
  - At its deepest, clumsiness becomes composure; once composure is strong enough, circumstances gradually begin to turn in his favor

### Part 6: Core Deliverables

#### Slide 13 — Hide Four Things, Cultivate Four Strengths

- **Layout**: vertical_list, four numbered principles (page_rhythm: dense)
- **Title**: Conceal four things, cultivate four kinds of strength
- **Visualization**: vertical_list
- **Content**:
  - 01 Conceal your emotions → Don’t let a few words provoke you
  - 02 Conceal your ambitions → Don’t let others prepare for you prematurely
  - 03 Conceal your capabilities → Don’t let others exhaust you too early
  - 04 Conceal your judgment → Don’t be forced to take sides before the situation is clear

#### Slide 14 — Closing Remarks

- **Layout**: Full-bleed distant mountain landscape + three centered lines of short phrases + byline（page_rhythm: anchor）
- **Title**: Ultimate Composure = Restrain the Need to Show Off × Keep Your Competitive Nerve Steady × Delay Gratification
- **Content**:
  - Stay steady, and you won't fear being temporarily underestimated
  - Stay discreet, and you won't fear a moment without applause
  - Be willing to wait, and you'll earn the right to let the results speak for themselves when the moment to act arrives

#### Slide 06 - LoRA 方法\n- **Layout**: i:
#### Slide 06 - The LoRA Method
- **Layout**: Image-as-canvas structural diagram + overlaid formulas (breathing)
- **Title**: Freeze W₀, Inject Low-Rank BA
- **Visualization**: (AI structural diagram reparam_diagram_cropped + formula_001/002)
- **Content**:
  - Constrain updates through low-rank decomposition: W₀ + ΔW = W₀ + BA
  - Forward pass: h = W₀x + BAx; W₀ is frozen during training, and only A and B are trained
  - A is initialized with Gaussian noise and B is set to zero → initial ΔW = 0

- **Content**:

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: Introduction

#### Slide 01 - Cover

- **Layout**: Full-screen background image + centered vertical title + figure silhouette
- **Title**: Lin Huiyin: The Architectural Master Overshadowed by a Literary Aura
- **Subtitle**: 70th Anniversary of Her Death · Rediscovering the Power of Women in Chinese Architectural History
- **Info**: Phoenix Space · 2025
- **Image**: cover_bg.png (full-screen background), lin_portrait.png (right side)

#### Slide 02 - Overview of Her Life and Career

- **Layout**: Horizontal timeline
- **Title**: The Life of an Architectural Master
- **Visualization**: timeline
- **Content**:
  - 1904 Born in Hangzhou
  - 1924 Went to the United States to study at the University of Pennsylvania
  - 1928 Married Liang Sicheng and returned to China
  - 1930 Joined the Society for Research in Chinese Architecture
  - 1932 Published her first architectural paper
  - 1937–1946 Displaced during wartime, she continued her research
  - 1949 Participated in the design of the national emblem
  - 1952 Participated in the design of the Monument to the People's Heroes
  - 1955 Died; her gravestone was inscribed "Tomb of Architect Lin Huiyin"

### Part 2: The Architect Lin Huiyin

#### Slide 03 - A Few Architectural Works (Part 1)

- **Layout**: Three-column card layout
- **Title**: Architectural practice after returning to China
- **Visualization**: icon_grid
- **Content**:
  - 1929 Liang Qichao Tomb Monument — Her first work after returning from abroad
  - 1929 Jilin University Stone Building — Participated in the design through the “Liang-Chen-Tong-Cai Construction Office”
  - 1929 Jihai Railway Terminal — Lin Huiyin designed the overall appearance, featuring a Gothic lion motif

#### Slide 04 - A Few Architectural Works (Part 2)

- **Layout**: Two-column split (4:6), image left and text right
- **Title**: Architectural Ideals Amidst War
- **Content**:
  - 1932 Peking University Geology Building and women’s dormitory — among China’s earliest introductions of Western modernist architecture
  - 1938 Yunnan University Yingqiu Hall — integrating elements of Yunnan vernacular architecture
  - 1938 Southwest Associated University campus buildings — “the most painful and aggrieved design of my life”
  - 1940 Kunming residence — the only house the two architects ever designed for themselves
- **Image**: kunming_site.png

#### Slide 05 - Landmark Works

- **Layout**: Two-column split (5:5), text left and image right
- **Title**: Architectural Imprints on the Nation’s Monuments
- **Content**:
  - 1950 Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery — designed the main architectural layout
  - 1952 Monument to the People’s Heroes — proposed creative revisions
  - Personally designed the complete ornamental patterns and garland reliefs on the pedestal
  - Based on Tang-dynasty style, expressing the aesthetics of traditional Chinese architecture
  - Only seven characters appear on the tombstone: Architect Lin Huiyin’s Tomb
- **Image**: monument.png

### Part 3: An Underestimated Academic Pioneer

#### Slide 06 - A Pioneer of Chinese Architectural Theory

- **Layout**: Two-column split (4:6), image left and text right
- **Title**: Her First Architectural Paper: A Stunning Debut
- **Content**:
  - 1932 *Several Characteristics of Chinese Architecture* — the first architectural theory paper published by a Chinese professional scholar
  - The first theoretical definition of the basic characteristics of China’s timber-frame structural system
  - Challenged Western scholars’ misinterpretations of Chinese architecture
  - Outlined a complete conceptual framework for Chinese architectural history
- **Image**: first_paper.png

#### Slide 07 - Original Concepts and Ahead-of-the-Curve Thinking

- **Layout**: Vertical key-point list
- **Title**: Overview of Academic Contributions
- **Visualization**: vertical_list
- **Content**:
  - The concept of “architectural meaning” — An original Chinese architectural philosophy in which architecture brings together technology, beauty, history, and human feeling
  - Introduction to *Examples of Qing-Style Construction* — Summarized the theoretical framework of Chinese architecture
  - Pioneer in vernacular architecture research — First in Chinese architectural circles to advocate the preservation of vernacular buildings
  - *References for Modern Housing Design* — Foresightedly proposed designing architecture for ordinary people after the war
  - First to offer a “General Introduction to Housing” course — Systematically taught modern housing design theory at Tsinghua University for the first time in 1949

### Part 4: Powerhouses and Spirit

#### Slide 08 - A Life Far More Astonishing Than the Rumors

- **Layout**: Two-column split (5:5), text left and image right
- **Title**: An Architectural Warrior Through the Flames of War
- **Content**:
  - Surveyed ancient architecture in remote valleys and wilderness, braving the elements without retreat
  - "Whatever Mr. Liang dared to climb, Mr. Lin dared to climb too"
  - Suffered a bout of pneumonia while displaced by war and never fully recovered afterward
  - Persisted with her illness, documenting Chinese architectural history stroke by stroke in remote towns
  - "What do I care about beauty or anything else? I still have so much to do!"
- **Image**: lin_survey.png

#### Slide 09 - The Work She Wants to Pursue for a Lifetime

- **Layout**: Introductory quote card + achievement summary
- **Title**: An Architect Beyond Question
- **Content**:
  - Introduction: "I myself have reached a considerable age, yet I have achieved nothing… I cannot help but feel sad" — from a letter to Hu Shi at age 28
  - Co-founded the architecture departments at Northeastern University and Tsinghua University with Liang Sicheng
  - Measured ancient architecture inch by inch in desolate regions
  - Devoted her final efforts to the national emblem and the Monument to the People's Heroes
  - She was not only a founder of the discipline, but also a pioneer in thought

#### Slide 10 - Conclusion

- **Layout**: Single centered column, quotation style
- **Title**: Architect Lin Huiyin's Tomb
- **Subtitle**: She Spent Her Life Proving That She Was an Architect in Every Sense of the Word
- **Content**:
  - Central gold vertical-line decoration
  - Quotation from the tombstone inscription
  - Tribute
  - Source information

zine 不是新东西，它有一百年的浪潮史。一九二零年代，哈莱姆文艺复兴时期就有黑: zines are nothing new; they have a century-long history of waves. In the 1920s, Black creators self-published booklets during the Harlem Renaissance. In the 1930s, science-fiction fans began producing fanzines, and the term "fanzine" was coined by Russ Chauvenet in 1940. In 1976, punk ignited zine culture as photocopiers became widespread, with Sniffin' Glue becoming an icon. In 1991, Riot Grrrl pushed zines into third-wave feminism; Kathleen Hanna's Bikini Kill zine remains a paradigm to this day. Today, zine culture is experiencing a revival through book fairs and library collections—it has always been here, just in different forms.

Take GPT-3's 175 billion parameters as an example: adapting it to each downstream task requires storing a complete full-parameter copy. If you have many tasks, the storage and switching cost becomes the number of tasks multiplied by 175 billion parameters—no longer merely "inconvenient," but a genuine deployment challenge.

Specifically, constrain the weight update to the product of two small matrices, B times A. During forward propagation, the input x passes through both the frozen W₀ and the bypass, and the two outputs are added together to produce h. During training, W₀ remains completely unchanged; only the two small matrices A and B are updated. Second, allow at least an hour; browsing itself is part of the product, and zoning out in front of the shelves is a legitimate form of consumption. 实现上有两个细节值得一提。第一是缩放:旁路的输出会乘上一个 alpha 除以 r: There are two implementation details worth mentioning. First, scaling: the output of the bypass is multiplied by a coefficient of alpha divided by r, with alpha set directly to the first r you try and not tuned separately afterward. This means you do not need to retune the hyperparameters every time you change the rank. Second, deployment: at launch, B can be explicitly multiplied by A and merged into the weights, yielding a W fully isomorphic to that of the original model, so no additional inference latency is introduced. Switching tasks is also simple: subtract the current BA and add the other task's B'A', with minimal overhead—ideal for online hot-swapping across multiple tasks.

接下来我们看一下 Agent 的标准骨架。基本上可以分成四层。最上面是感知层，负: Next, let’s look at the standard Agent architecture. It can basically be divided into four layers. At the top is the perception layer, responsible for input parsing, multimodal fusion, and context-window management. The second is the reasoning layer, which handles decision-making paradigms such as Plan, ReAct, Tree-of-Thought, and Reflection. The third is the action layer, translating the model’s decisions into tool calls, function execution, and API orchestration. At the bottom is the memory layer, including short-term context, long-term vector stores, and task-level caches. Each layer has its own engineering pitfalls, but with the right framework, every layer can be refined and replaced independently.

最后做个总结。从方法本身看,低秩适配等于参数高效、零额外推理延迟,再加上质量持平: Let's wrap up. In terms of the method itself, low-rank adaptation means parameter efficiency, zero additional inference latency, and equal or even better quality. From an engineering perspective, it allows a single pretrained base model to host many tasks, with LoRA modules hot-swapped as needed, substantially reducing deployment costs. In terms of industry impact, LoRA is open source and has become one of the cornerstones of today's efficient large-model fine-tuning, or PEFT, ecosystem. Its greatest value is that it means we no longer have to choose between efficiency and quality. Thank you, everyone.

I hope the framework I shared today can help you on your journey. Thank you, everyone.

This year, China is vigorously promoting the urban-renewal philosophy of “inspection before renewal.” As of November 2025, 297 prefecture-level-and-above cities and more than 150 county-level cities nationwide had launched urban inspections, focusing on issues such as hidden structural safety risks in residential buildings, illegal construction, and unauthorized alterations to load-bearing walls. From inspection to design, from coordination to regeneration, the future of supertall buildings lies in meticulous, fine-grained renovation. From pursuing height to building depth—this is a microcosm of urban development returning to rationality and pursuing high quality. Thank you, everyone.

理解了四层骨架之后，下一个常见问题是：到底用哪种模式。简单说有三种。Workfl: After understanding the four-layer skeleton, the next common question is: which mode should you use? Simply put, there are three. Workflow is a fixed-path DAG where the LLM only fills in the blanks—predictable, easy to debug, and suitable for deterministic tasks. Agent has a dynamic path, letting the model decide the next step at runtime. It is the most common approach and what most projects actually do, making it suitable for semi-structured exploratory tasks. Multi-Agent involves collaboration among multiple roles, splitting Planner, Critic, and Worker into concurrent collaborators. It offers the most flexibility but also the highest complexity, so use it only when truly long-horizon tasks are needed. For the vast majority of production scenarios, starting with Agent is enough.

A zine is therefore a self-made publication produced in extremely small quantities, with content entirely controlled by its author. It can be handwritten, collaged, a comic, or a manifesto. The key boundary is this: once a zine enters mass distribution and an editorial process, it is no longer a zine.

第一道是性能不稳定，多步推理一叠加，每一步五到十个百分点的抖动累计起来，整体成功: The first challenge is unstable performance. As multiple reasoning steps accumulate, fluctuations of five to ten percentage points at each step can cause the overall success rate to fall off a cliff, while P95 latency often increases five- to tenfold. The second is unpredictable cost. For the same task, token consumption can vary five- to fiftyfold across different context lengths, with long-tail tasks especially likely to blow through the budget. The third is the lack of a closed-loop quality process. It is often unclear whether a failure comes from the model, the prompt, or the data, and without regression testing, every prompt change feels like a gamble. These are the three hurdles that most projects encounter first.
第七站，阿布扎比。这是建筑鬼才弗兰克·盖里留给世界的最后巨作。盖里在二零二五年十: Seventh stop: Abu Dhabi. This is the final masterpiece left to the world by architectural maverick Frank Gehry. Gehry passed away in December 2025, while the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi, to which he devoted nearly two decades, is expected to open in 2026. Irregular curves, fluid folds, and highly dramatic geometric forms define the building, along with a shading system tailored to the desert’s extreme climate. Its metal façade shifts in texture as the sunlight moves. As the deconstructivist master’s swan song, this building offers Gehry’s final interpretation of his belief that architecture has no boundaries and creativity no limits.
第三个案例跳到纽约。这是 One Wall Street，曼哈顿金融区一座装饰艺: The third case takes us to New York. This is One Wall Street, a 1931 Art Deco skyscraper in Manhattan’s Financial District, designed by renowned architect Ralph Walker and rising 50 stories. It has now been converted from an office building into 566 apartments, ranging from studios to four-bedroom units. As we see on this tour, the vast majority of successfully converted high-rises were formerly office or commercial buildings. The reason is practical: these buildings generally have stronger structures than residential properties, offering greater flexibility and making it easier to introduce new uses.
第三站，台北淡水河口。这座二零二六年五月十二日通车的淡江大桥，是扎哈·哈迪德生前: Third stop: the Tamsui River estuary in Taipei. Opened to traffic on May 12, 2026, the Tamsui River Bridge is one of the final projects completed by the firm Zaha Hadid was part of during her lifetime. Stretching 920 meters, it is the longest-span single-tower asymmetric cable-stayed bridge of its kind in the world. Most moving of all, after numerous rounds of design challenges, the project ultimately realized Zaha’s nearly idealized vision with close to 100% fidelity. Though the master is gone, her architectural spirit of breaking boundaries and refusing limits continues to thrive in this bridge.
第二站，米兰。这是二零二六年米兰科尔蒂纳冬奥会唯一的新建永久场馆——奇普菲尔德设: Second stop: Milan. This is the only new permanent venue built for the 2026 Milan–Cortina Winter Olympics—the San Giulia Ice Hockey Arena, designed by David Chipperfield. The elliptical venue, which seats 16,000 spectators, echoes the ancient Roman amphitheaters of a city with 2,000 years of history. 让我们单独看一下 Müller-Brockmann 这个人。他 1914 年生于: Let’s take a closer look at Müller-Brockmann himself. Born in 1914 in the small Swiss town of Rapperswil, about 40 kilometers from Zurich, he opened an independent studio in Zurich in 1936 at the age of 22, working across three fields: graphic design, exhibitions, and photography. The real turning point came in 1950, when he began designing the Musica Viva poster series for Zurich’s Tonhalle, using pure geometric elements—circles, arcs, lines, and rectangles—to express musical structures in abstract form. To this day, the series remains a textbook example of constructivist poster design. In 1957, he became a professor at the Zurich School of Applied Arts. In 1958, together with three like-minded designers, he founded the trilingual journal Neue Grafik, formally bringing Swiss ideas to the international design community. In 1981, he published Grid Systems in Graphic Design—the foundational text for today’s lecture. He died in Unterengstringen in 1996 at the age of 82.
让我用穆勒·布罗克曼最常被引用的一句话结束——网格不是限制，是自由的语法。The: Let me close with Müller-Brockmann’s most frequently quoted line: the grid is not a constraint. It is a grammar of freedom. If you take away just one thing today, I hope it is this: when a designer complains that the grid limits creativity, what they are really complaining about is that they have not yet learned how to use it; when a designer truly masters the grid, what they gain is not confinement, but a universal framework capable of supporting almost any content, style, or medium. Thank you, everyone.

讲了这么多概念，我们来动手。一张 A4 纸就能折出一本八页的 zine，全部步骤: After all these concepts, let’s get hands-on. A single sheet of A4 paper can be folded into an eight-page zine in just four steps. First, fold it in half along the long edge, then along the short edge, and once more along the centerline to create eight rectangles; second, cut from the folded edge to the center point—just one cut; third, push both ends of the paper toward the center, and it will automatically fold into a small booklet; fourth, fill it with content—there are no rules. The only hard constraint is that the zine’s total page count must be a multiple of 4.
讲完 zine 的简史，我们看它的灵魂工艺：Risograph。Risograp: After the brief history of the zine, let’s look at its soul: Risograph printing. Risograph is a duplicator product launched in 1986 by Riso Kagaku Corporation, a Japanese company founded in 1946. It was originally created to provide an affordable, eco-friendly printing solution in postwar Japan, but decades later it became a core tool of independent art. Its four defining visual features—limited palettes, misregistered colors, halftone dots, and overprinted ink—are all technical limitations, but artists turned those limitations into a visual language. This page uses misregistration and halftones simulated in SVG.
讲完了人，讲三款字体。Akzidenz-Grotesk，1896 年由柏林的 B: After the people, let’s look at three typefaces. Akzidenz-Grotesk was released in 1896 by the Berthold type foundry in Berlin—the first commercial sans-serif typeface in the modern sense. It predates Helvetica by a full 61 years and established the fundamental tone of sans-serif aesthetics. Helvetica was designed by Miedinger and Hoffmann in 1957. Its name literally means “Swiss,” from the Latin Helvetia. Neutral, objective, and exceptionally legible, it became the most widely disseminated typeface of the twentieth century. Also in 1957, Adrian Frutiger created Univers. For the first time, he systematized “family, weight, and width” through a two-dimensional numbering system with 21 weights, making it the ancestor of the modern type family structure. Within a single year, Switzerland produced two decisive typefaces—an eruption of an era.
讲完工具，下面这页是我个人觉得最重要的一页：上下文工程。模型每天都在变，提示词也: After style itself, this page is, in my view, the most important one: context engineering. Models change every day, and prompts are constantly being adjusted, but what truly determines whether an Agent is intelligent is what it sees at each step—in other words, its context. Around this core, at least six things need to be done well: retrieval must be reliable, reranking precise, truncation selective, memory divided into short- and long-term, tool descriptions specific enough, and system prompts clear about persona, output format, and safety rules. If context engineering is poorly done, even a powerful model cannot be saved.
讲完风格本身，看它的影响。从 1960 年代开始，瑞士理性被输出到四个方向。第一: After style itself, let’s look at its influence. Beginning in the 1960s, Swiss rationalism spread in four directions. The first was corporate VI. Under Paul Rand, IBM, Knoll, Lufthansa, Olivetti, Braun, and a series of other major companies turned Swiss rationalism into an industry called “identity systems”; Müller-Brockmann himself served as an IBM consultant from 1967. The second was airport and subway signage—the New York subway’s 1966 Unimark design manual, Frutiger’s typeface for Charles de Gaulle Airport, and Otl Aicher’s work for the Munich Olympics. The legibility of public spaces is a direct extension of Swiss rationalism. The third was publishing, from Switzerland’s Du magazine to Eye, Domus, and Wallpaper, which remain models of cultural publishing to this day. The fourth was design education. Through Swiss-trained teachers at schools such as Yale, RISD, and Cooper Union, the Basel and Zurich teaching traditions passed this visual grammar down from one generation to the next.

First, choose a topic you genuinely care about. It doesn’t need to be grand; cats, breakfast, or your commute will do. Second, fold an A4 sheet using the method taught on page seven—it takes thirty seconds. Third, fill these eight pages; handwriting, collage, or photocopies of old photos are all fine. The first one should be rough. Fourth, print ten copies: give five to friends and send five to independent bookstores. The moment you send out your first copy, you become a zine publisher—the threshold isn’t commercial registration, an ISBN, or sales. It’s the second you send it out.

First, objectivity comes before expression — conveying information takes priority over the designer’s personal emotions. Second, the mathematical grid serves as the framework — columns, rows, spacing, and modules are all derived from basic units. Third, asymmetrical composition — rejecting the central authority implied by classical symmetry. Fourth, sans-serif typefaces. Fifth, flush left and ragged right, with even letter spacing. Sixth, objective photography replaces decorative illustration. 风格从纸面跳到屏幕只用了二十年，但语法没有变。2008 年，Nathan Smi: It took just twenty years for the style to jump from paper to screen, but the grammar remained unchanged. In 2008, Nathan Smith created the 960 Grid System: 12 columns, 960 pixels wide, bringing grid-based design systematically to the Web for the first time. In 2011, Twitter open-sourced Bootstrap. With the same 12-column structure, it brought modular grids to front-end developers around the world. In 2017, CSS Grid gained native support in all major browsers, making the modular grid a foundational part of the Web platform for the first time. By the 2020s, Material Design, Apple's Human Interface Guidelines, Adobe Spectrum, and Microsoft Fluent had extended major corporations' visual identities onto screens, transforming rule sets into component libraries. In a word—from printed posters to CSS Grid, the medium changed, but the same four elements remained: modules, columns, white space, and mathematical proportions.
